## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (five Suggestion findings, no checklist failures)

The PR is ready to merge: all 63 checklist items passed, every one of the 20 acceptance criteria is itemized and verified, and the four reviewers raised only Suggestion-level points, all below the `critical` threshold.
Rule applied: rule 6 — findings below the threshold remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

Findings four and five name the same sentence in `docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md` but carry different `defect_signature` kinds (`comment_drift` and `documented_falsehood`), so they do not formally corroborate; they describe one defect.

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (5)

<details><summary>5 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py` lines 73-78: two places decide whether a statement is a read. The runner stamps `READ_RESULT_ATTR` on a read frame, so "runner read, tool reports a read" is covered. The write-branch `rows_affected` frames in the SQLite, MySQL and Postgres runners carry no marker, so a tool whose `dialect` differs from the runner's could show a `rows_affected` frame as a result table. `RunSqlTool.dialect` is public, defaults to `None` and is not validated when the tool is built; a misspelled dialect only logs a WARNING twice per `execute` and falls back to no dialect. `build_agent` passes the URL dialect, so no built-in wiring reaches this. (raised by 1/4 agents)
2. `docs/internal/agent/tool-scratch-storage.md` lines 7 and 14 say only statements `is_read_shaped` classifies as read-shaped get a result table, and that "Only statements that are not read-shaped get the row-count summary". `run_sql.py` line 78 also builds the table when the runner's frame carries `READ_RESULT_ATTR`, whatever the tool's own classification; `test_rows_from_runner_with_other_dialect_are_kept` and `test_empty_read_from_runner_with_other_dialect_reports_no_rows` pin that second path. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: internal doc sentence, making it true changes no output; git grep of *.sh/*.py/*.jq/*.yml/*.toml/.github for the path and the sentence found no reader; no workflow or mkdocs config publishes docs/internal -->
3. `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 91-94: the modified `is_read_shaped` docstring still calls it a "Cheap first-token check". `first_sql_keyword` now tokenizes the whole statement, so a `TokenError` anywhere after a valid leading `SELECT` (for example `SELECT n FROM widgets /* note`) gives `""` and `False`, as `test_is_read_shaped_by_dialect` pins. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: docstring wording, making it true changes no output; git grep for the phrase found only readonly.py:91; the docstring is never printed -->
4. `docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md` line 302 says `query_type` is "the leading SQL keyword" and is `""` "when no keyword leads the statement". `first_sql_keyword` also returns an unquoted identifier, uppercased (the `TokenType.VAR` branch); `test_unquoted_identifier_is_returned` pins `"foo bar"` → `"FOO"`. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: internal doc sentence, making it true changes no output; git grep of tooling found no reader of the sentence; docs/internal is not published -->
5. `docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md` line 302: the same `query_type` sentence, reported as a documented falsehood: a statement led by a bare identifier gets that identifier, not `""`, as `query_type`; the function's own docstring at `readonly.py` lines 50-51 says so. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: internal doc sentence, making it true changes no output; git grep of tooling found no reader of the sentence; docs/internal is not published -->

</details>

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `first_sql_keyword` returns `SELECT` for a `SELECT` preceded by any mix of leading whitespace, opening parentheses, `--` comment lines and `/* … */` comments (at minimum `-- note` + newline + `SELECT 1`, `/* note */ SELECT 1`, `/* a */ (SELECT 1)`, `( -- a` + newline + `SELECT 1)`) and for a keyword touching a symbol (at minimum `SELECT*FROM t`, `SELECT/* c */1`), with no dialect and with each of `sqlite`, `postgres` and `mysql`; it returns `WITH` for the same prefixes before a `WITH` query; and every existing `TestFirstSqlKeyword` case keeps its expected value.
- [ ] `first_sql_keyword("/* a /* b */ c */ SELECT 1", "postgres")` returns `SELECT`, and with `mysql` or `sqlite` it returns `C`, matching how each engine ends the comment.
- [ ] `first_sql_keyword("# c\nSELECT 1", "mysql")` returns `SELECT`; with `postgres`, `sqlite` or no dialect it returns `""`.
- [ ] `first_sql_keyword` returns `""` for, at minimum, the SQL texts `'x' AS a`, `1 AS a` and `"t"` (a quoted identifier), each with `postgres`, and for empty and whitespace-only SQL; and `first_sql_keyword(sql, "no-such-dialect")` equals `first_sql_keyword(sql)` for every input this criterion and the three above name.
- [ ] `first_sql_keyword` returns `""` for a statement sqlglot's tokenizer cannot tokenize, with no dialect and with each of `sqlite`, `postgres` and `mysql` (at minimum `-- c\nSELECT 'x` and `/* unterminated SELECT 1`), and a unit test pins that result; an exception from the tokenizer other than `TokenError` propagates; `first_sql_keyword` uses only sqlglot's public API; and `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` contains no `_strip_leading_comments` and no regex, `.split()` or `startswith` test on SQL text in `first_sql_keyword`.
- [ ] `is_read_shaped("SELECT n FROM widgets # x\r'\n", "mysql")` is `True`, and `assert_select_only` accepts that statement with `dialect="mysql"`.
- [ ] Every existing `is_introspection_query` test keeps its expected value except the three unterminated comment-led `SHOW` cases of `test_own_engine_catalogs_detected` (`# tables\n/* again */ SHOW 'abc` and `/* c */ SHOW 'abc` on `mysql`, `-- c\nSHOW 'abc` on `postgres`), which now expect `False`, with a test comment saying that the read-only guard fails closed on the same input and the database rejects it, so it never returns rows; `is_introspection_query("#x\nSHOW 'abc", dialect="postgres")` is still `False`; and `is_introspection_query("# c\nSHOW TABLES")` with no dialect is `False`.
- [ ] `is_introspection_query` returns `False` for, at minimum, these data queries whose CTE name starts with a catalog prefix: `WITH pg_recent AS (SELECT 1 AS n) SELECT * FROM pg_recent` and `WITH PG_RECENT AS (SELECT 1 AS n) SELECT * FROM pg_recent` on `postgres`, and `WITH sqlite_recent AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM sqlite_recent` on `sqlite`; and it still returns `True` for, at minimum, `WITH x AS (SELECT * FROM pg_class) SELECT * FROM x` and `WITH pg_recent AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM pg_recent JOIN pg_class ON true` on `postgres`, `DESCRIBE information_schema.tables` on `mysql`, and `WITH sqlite_master AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM sqlite_master, main.sqlite_master` on `sqlite`.
- [ ] When identifier normalization or scope analysis raises any exception, `is_introspection_query` excludes no node and logs the exception type: with `traverse_scope` patched to raise, `WITH pg_recent AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM pg_recent` on `postgres` is `True`, and a unit test pins it.
- [ ] A comment-led `SELECT` and a `SELECT*FROM` read, each run through `SqliteRunner` over more rows than `max_rows`, return exactly `max_rows` rows of the selected columns, marked truncated, not a `rows_affected` frame; the MySQL runner, driven through a fake `pymysql`, executes `# c` + newline + `SELECT 1` on its `SSDictCursor` streaming cursor; and the Postgres runner, driven through a fake `psycopg2`, executes `-- c` + newline + `SELECT 1` on its named (server-side) cursor.
